The TADS system was developed under NASA Contract NAS3-25950.
TADS couples the ADPAC throughflow solver with the RVCQ3D quasi-3D blade-to-blade solver.
The GUI simplifies user input and automates the many tasks required to perform turbomachinery analysis and design.
TADS begins the analysis with the throughflow calculation, using the mean camber line and Carter's deviation angle rule to set the initial mean stream surface.
The ADPAC throughflow solver was modified to include blade force and blockage terms in the governing equations.
TADS uses a file naming convention, data standards, and shared routines/data to enable modularity and maintainability.
The TADS system was verified using the NASA Rotor 67 test case.
The TADS system was designed to incorporate modern CFD techniques into the traditional turbomachinery design approach.
The TADS GUI controls the complete analysis, allowing the user to select program modules, input data, and run the analysis on remote hosts.
The TADS system was developed to enable new modules to be added to perform any of the tasks without major coding effort.
The TADS system is an amalgamation of many different programs under a single GUI.
The TADS system requires four inputs: a case name, a Cartesian description of the airfoil, a description of the meridional flow path, and aerodynamic data.
The TADS system minimizes interpolation errors between the various airfoil representations by using normalized airfoil chord when necessary.
The TADS system defaults to equal axial spacing within the three blocks of the throughflow grid (upstream, within the airfoil row, and downstream).
The TADS system was designed to enable alternative solvers or grid generators to be easily incorporated into the framework.
